title: API http.Server omits ReadTimeout, leaving stalled request bodies without a read deadline
description: newAPIServer (go/cmd/api/main.go:154-163) sets ReadHeaderTimeout=10s, WriteTimeout=6m (reset.DefaultRefinalizeDrainTimeout plus apiRecoveryResponseMargin), and IdleTimeout=120s, but leaves ReadTimeout at its zero value. In net/http the header deadline applies only around header parsing; for the body phase the conn sets the read deadline to wholeReqDeadline, which stays the zero time when ReadTimeout is 0 (stdlib server.go:1038-1041 and :1103 at go1.27.3). A client that sends headers with Content-Length and then pauses between body bytes pins its connection, its per-connection serve goroutine, and the bufio read buffers with no deadline until the client resumes or SIGTERM triggers the Shutdown drain (default 30s via ESHU_API_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT). IdleTimeout=120s does not rescue the body phase because it applies only between requests on a keep-alive connection. The sibling status plane (go/internal/runtime/http_server.go:64) shares the same header-only omission.
root_cause: The http.Server literal in newAPIServer never assigns ReadTimeout, so the stdlib body-phase read deadline is the zero time and stalled body reads are unbounded.
intended_behavior: With a finite ReadTimeout, the stdlib bounds the entire request read (headers plus body): a stalled body read fails with an i/o timeout once the deadline passes, releasing the connection and its serve goroutine promptly. ReadHeaderTimeout alone bounds only the header parse.

trace.description: srv := newAPIServer(addr, handler) builds the single API-plane server that ListenAndServe runs; the handler chain is assembled at main.go:92-100.
The server literal sets ReadHeaderTimeout, WriteTimeout, and IdleTimeout but not ReadTimeout, so the conn-level body deadline stays zero.
The returned server is served by ListenAndServe; each stalled body read holds its conn and serve goroutine indefinitely under the zero whole-request deadline.

evidence.description: Server literal: ReadHeaderTimeout=10s, WriteTimeout=6m, IdleTimeout=120s; ReadTimeout absent (zero).
TestAPIServerWriteTimeoutOutlivesRefinalizeDrain pins only the write bound; no test grades a body-phase ReadTimeout.
Status-plane sibling sets ReadHeaderTimeout only, the same header-only posture.

conditions.description: Any client able to reach the API listener; no credential is needed to occupy a connection mid-body.
The stall is observable while the client pauses between body bytes; resuming or closing releases the goroutine.

execution.attacker_perspective: A plain TCP client speaking HTTP/1.1 to the API listener.
payloads: POST /api/v1/... with Content-Length set, headers sent, then byte-by-byte body writes with 4s pauses between bytes.
Same sequence with the server configured with ReadTimeout=3s as the bounded control.
instructions: Build a scratch Go program that constructs an http.Server with the exact timeout set from go/cmd/api/main.go:154-163 (ReadHeaderTimeout=10s, WriteTimeout=6m, IdleTimeout=120s, ReadTimeout unset) and a handler that reads the body.
Open 3 sockets, send headers, then pause 4s between body bytes; record per-request completion wall time.
Repeat with ReadTimeout=3s and compare.
execution.observed_result: With ReadTimeout=0 each handler completed only after the full pause (wall 4s/8s/12s, no deadline error). With ReadTimeout=3s every stalled body read was reaped at 3s with an i/o timeout, releasing conn and goroutine. go test ./cmd/api -count=1 exits 0 (artifact agents/verifier-readtimeout/artifacts/repro3.go).

remediation.strategy: Add a finite ReadTimeout to the API-plane server literal sized to the largest expected request body under the repo-scale performance contract, keeping the existing header/write/idle bounds.

code_changes.fixed_code:
srv := &http.Server{
	Addr:              addr,
	Handler:           handler,
	ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
	ReadTimeout:       30 * time.Second,
	WriteTimeout:      reset.DefaultRefinalizeDrainTimeout + apiRecoveryResponseMargin,
	IdleTimeout:       120 * time.Second,
}

likelihood.reason: Stalls are visible and self-releasing on resume; the process still serves between pauses, and the default deployment drain bounds total occupancy.

impact.reason: Per-stalled-connection goroutine and buffer retention only; no data corruption and no wrong results; released on resume or shutdown.

confidence.reason: Both arms of the comparison were executed locally under the same harness at go1.27.3, and the stdlib deadline semantics were read from the pinned toolchain source.

title: CLI .env Load() ignores bufio.Scanner.Err(), silently truncating the parse on tokens over 64 KiB
description: go/internal/cli/config/env.go:69-81 runs the line scan without checking scanner.Err(). A value token longer than the 64 KiB bufio default makes Scan() stop with bufio.ErrTooLong, yet Load() returns the partial map with a nil error. The sibling runtime parser (go/internal/runtime/api_key.go:155) checks scanner.Err() on the same format, so the two parsers of one file format diverge. Because SetValue rewrites the whole file from the truncated map, the keys after the over-long token are permanently lost on the next write.
root_cause: Load() returns the partial map without consulting scanner.Err(), so bufio.ErrTooLong is indistinguishable from a clean end of file.
intended_behavior: Load() reports the scan error like the sibling parser, so callers can distinguish a complete parse from a truncated one and avoid persisting a lossy rewrite.

trace.description: Scans the operator .env file line by line with bufio.Scanner.
Returns the map built so far with a nil error even when Scan stopped early on ErrTooLong.

evidence.description: Scan loop; no scanner.Err() check before return.
Sibling parser checks scanner.Err() on the same .env format, proving the intended contract.

conditions.description: An operator .env containing a single value token longer than 65535 bytes (for example a large inline certificate).

execution.attacker_perspective: The CLI process reading its own .env file.
instructions: Write a package test that seeds the three-key .env above, calls config.Load, and asserts the returned map and error.
Then call SetValue and re-read the file to show the persisted truncation.
execution.observed_result: Load() returns exactly {K1:1} with nil error; AFTER and LONG are absent. SetValue(NEW,1) rewrites the file to K1=1 and NEW=1 only, so AFTER is permanently lost. The raw scanner reports bufio.ErrTooLong. Existing package tests stay green (ok internal/cli/config, exit 0; artifact agents/verifier-clienv/artifacts/repro.go).

remediation.strategy: Check scanner.Err() after the loop and return it, matching the sibling parser in api_key.go.

likelihood.reason: Only tokens above 64 KiB trigger it; most .env files use shorter values, though inline certificates are plausible.

impact.reason: Silent loss of the trailing keys of one operator config file; recoverable by re-writing the file.

confidence.reason: Reproduced independently with a package test under go1.27.3 and cross-checked against the sibling parser's error handling.

title: CLI .env SetValue performs an unlocked non-atomic Load-then-WriteFile, losing keys under concurrent writers
description: go/internal/cli/config/env.go:154 implements SetValue as a full-file rewrite from a freshly loaded map with no lock, no flock, and no rename-based atomic replace (the flock in api_key.go guards only that file's own state). Two SetValue calls that each Load before either WriteFile produce last-writer-wins: keys added by the first writer are absent from the second writer's snapshot and disappear from the final file. A truncated write is also possible mid-rewrite since os.WriteFile is not atomic.
root_cause: SetValue reads and rewrites the whole file as two unguarded steps, so the pair is not atomic across concurrent writers.
intended_behavior: Either the persisted .env equals the union of committed intents, or the read-modify-write is serialized (per-file lock) and crash-atomic (temp file plus rename), so no concurrent writer loses keys.

trace.description: Loads the current map from disk.
os.WriteFile replaces the file from that snapshot with no lock and no rename swap.

evidence.description: Load snapshot taken immediately before the rewrite.
Bare os.WriteFile; no flock, no temp-and-rename.

conditions.description: Two CLI invocations writing the same profile .env overlap (for example scripted setup followed by a manual config set).

execution.attacker_perspective: The CLI process itself; no remote principal involved.
payloads: Two SetValue calls prepared from one shared pre-write Load snapshot: FIRST=k1 and SECOND=k2.
instructions: In a scratch package test, Load twice before any write, SetValue(FIRST), SetValue(SECOND), then re-read the file.
Assert which keys survive.
execution.observed_result: The final file keeps SECOND and loses FIRST (last-writer-wins), independently reproduced; the 65537-byte truncation case from the sibling fingerprint reproduces in the same harness. Package suite stays green (go test ./internal/cli/config/ -count=1, exit 0; artifact agents/verifier-rewrite/artifacts/verify_repro_test.go).

remediation.strategy: Make the rewrite crash-atomic with a same-directory temp file plus os.Rename, which also gives readers a consistent old-or-new view; a per-file flock if a full read-modify-write serialization is wanted.

likelihood.reason: Requires two overlapping SetValue calls; typical CLI use is sequential.

impact.reason: Loss of one writer's keys in one operator config file; self-healing by re-setting values.

confidence.reason: Deterministic two-snapshot sequence reproduced in a scratch test with a fixed expected file content.

title: boundedReadOnlyCypher accepts a non-terminal first LIMIT, so the documented 1000-row cap never reaches the driver
description: explicitCypherLimit (go/internal/query/codequery/cypher.go:297) returns ok as soon as it sees a LIMIT token, without checking that it is the last one, and boundedReadOnlyCypher therefore appends no terminal cap when the first LIMIT sits inside a WITH clause. For 'MATCH (n) WITH n LIMIT 1 MATCH (m) RETURN m' the executed statement is byte-identical to the input and the final result set is uncapped (only the 4096-byte query cap and the 30s timeout bind it). The visualization twin boundedVisualizationCypher is correct: it uses terminalCypherLimit (cypher.go:241-244) and appends LIMIT 6 / LIMIT 1001 on the same shapes, pinned by TestHandleVisualizeQuery_InnerLimitGetsTerminalCap.
root_cause: explicitCypherLimit returns at the first LIMIT token without a terminality check, so a mid-query LIMIT suppresses the terminal row cap.
intended_behavior: The executed statement always carries a terminal row cap: a trailing LIMIT is kept, any non-terminal LIMIT leaves the appended cypherMaxResultRows cap in place.

trace.description: The single call site of explicitCypherLimit inside the read path for execute_cypher_query.
Returns ok on the first LIMIT token found; no check that it terminates the statement, so no cap is appended.

evidence.description: First-LIMIT acceptance without terminality check.
terminalCypherLimit, the correct twin used by the visualization path.
TestHandleVisualizeQuery_InnerLimitGetsTerminalCap pins the twin but nothing pins the execute path.

conditions.description: A caller-supplied read-only Cypher statement whose first LIMIT appears in a WITH clause before the final RETURN.

execution.attacker_perspective: An authenticated API/MCP caller of execute_cypher_query.
payloads: MATCH (n) WITH n LIMIT 1 MATCH (m) RETURN m
MATCH (a) WITH a LIMIT 1000 MATCH (b) RETURN a,b
instructions: Port explicitCypherLimit and boundedReadOnlyCypher verbatim into a scratch main.
Print the executed statement for both payloads and compare with the input.
Run the same shapes through boundedVisualizationCypher as the control.
execution.observed_result: Both non-terminal-LIMIT inputs reach the driver byte-identical with no appended LIMIT, while the visualization twin appends LIMIT 6 / LIMIT 1001 on the same shapes. go test ./internal/query/codequery/ ./internal/query/codemodel/ -count=1 exits 0 (artifact agents/hunter-query/artifacts/unit1-result.json).

remediation.strategy: Use the terminal-aware scan for the execute path too: replace the explicitCypherLimit call at cypher.go:152 with terminalCypherLimit so only a trailing LIMIT suppresses the appended cap.

likelihood.reason: Only statements with an inner non-terminal LIMIT take the uncapped path; most authored queries end with a trailing LIMIT.

impact.reason: One query returns more rows than the documented 1000-row budget; bounded anyway by the 4096-byte query cap and the 30s driver timeout.

confidence.reason: Verbatim local port reproduced both the uncapped inputs and the capped twin; package suites green.

title: Headerless API requests are served open when only the identity store is configured
description: authEnforcementConfigured (go/cmd/api/auth_enforcement.go:42-48) treats the auth plane as configured only when apiKey, fileResolver, or oidcResolver is non-nil. The identity-store resolver, wired unconditionally at go/cmd/api/wiring.go:155 and first in the credential chain at :211, is not counted. Under identity-only wiring, a headerless request falls through the auth gate (go/internal/query/auth.go:187-190) without a ContextWithAuthContext, and RepositoryAccessFilterFromContext takes its !ok branch (go/internal/query/querycontract/repository_authz_context.go:26-27) yielding AllScopes:true, so data routes answer with unfiltered reads. The posture is pinned by TestAPIAuthBootstrapIdentityOnlyServesHeaderlessOpen and the auth_headerless_bypass tests.
root_cause: The three-knob predicate that decides whether authentication is enforced omits the identity resolver, so an identity-only deployment behaves as an unauthenticated open plane for headerless requests.
intended_behavior: Whenever any credential source can answer a request, the headerless fall-through should be closed: either a missing credential is rejected, or the identity resolver's presence flips the posture to enforced.

trace.description: Single HTTP auth gate for the API plane.
Counts only apiKey, fileResolver, oidcResolver; the identity resolver is invisible to the predicate.
With enforcement not configured, a headerless request proceeds without an AuthContext.
Missing AuthContext yields AllScopes:true, so repository reads are unfiltered.

evidence.description: Three-knob predicate definition.
Identity resolver wired unconditionally, ahead of the counted knobs.
TestAPIAuthBootstrapIdentityOnlyServesHeaderlessOpen pins headerless 200 under identity-only wiring.

conditions.description: Deployment configured with the identity-token store only (no API key file, no OIDC).

execution.attacker_perspective: Any client on the API listener network.
payloads: GET /api/v1/... with no Authorization header against an identity-only deployment
Same path with the seeded identity token (control: 200) and a wrong token (control: 401)
instructions: Run the pinned suites: go test ./cmd/api -run AuthEnforcement|Headerless and go test ./internal/query -run Headerless|EnforcementConstructor.
execution.observed_result: 5 PASS in cmd/api incl. TestAPIAuthBootstrapIdentityOnlyServesHeaderlessOpen (seeded identity-token row: headerless 200, matching token 200, wrong token 401); 7 PASS in internal/query incl. TestAuthMiddlewareEnforcementConstructorOpenWhenNotEnforced; exit 0 (artifact agents/hunter-authn2/artifacts/cmdapi-headerless-open.txt).

remediation.strategy: Count the identity resolver in the enforcement predicate, but only when the identity store is non-empty so the demo-config test keeps its headerless-open behavior.

likelihood.reason: Identity-only wiring is a supported minimal configuration and the headerless path is exercised by the pinned tests themselves.

impact.reason: Unfiltered reads on the data plane for headerless requests in that configuration; each credential-carrying request still gets its scoped filter.

confidence.reason: Both governing tests executed green on the reviewed tree and the predicate, fall-through, and !ok branch were read directly at the cited lines.

title: Browser-session workspace switch rebinds by session hash without a subject or tenant membership predicate
description: switchBrowserSessionWorkspaceQuery (go/internal/storage/postgres/browser_sessions_schema.go:369-410) keys only on session_hash and validates the target pair against the active non-tombstoned catalog, with revoked_at IS NULL, all_scopes=true, and both expiries checked. It carries no sess.tenant_id/workspace_id equality against the stored row and no subject_id_hash term, and the handler (go/internal/query/browser_session_handler.go:264-284) forwards the body pair verbatim. After the switch, the resolve projection re-anchors on the rewritten row (schema :220-249), so subsequent identity-bound reads use the rebound pair. The in-tree doc comment records the same residual (#6450 item 4 at go/internal/query/auth_browser_session_route_policy.go:297-304).
root_cause: The UPDATE that swaps the active workspace binds solely on session_hash, so the tenant/workspace pair is not checked against the row's own membership.
intended_behavior: A context switch should rebind only to a workspace the session's subject is a member of in the session's own tenant, making the post-switch anchor provably consistent with the pre-switch membership.

trace.description: Parses the body pair {tenant_id, workspace_id} and forwards it verbatim to the store.
Single UPDATE keyed on session_hash with catalog validation only; no subject/membership predicate.

evidence.description: Query text: keys on session_hash; ws.tenant_id and ws.workspace_id come from the request pair.
TestBrowserSessionStoreSwitchesActiveWorkspaceByHash pins the single-UPDATE shape via a recording fake.
In-tree note records the unbound-pair residual (#6450 item 4).

conditions.description: A valid browser session id plus its CSRF token (the pair a logged-in principal already holds).
Target pair exists in the active non-tombstoned catalog.

execution.attacker_perspective: An authenticated browser-session principal against POST /api/v1 session routes.
payloads: Body {tenant_id, workspace_id} pair differing from the row's stored anchor with the correct session hash and CSRF token.
instructions: Run: go test ./internal/storage/postgres/ -run TestBrowserSessionStoreSwitchesActiveWorkspaceByHash -count=1.
execution.observed_result: PASS, exit 0 (ok github.com/eshu-hq/eshu/go/internal/storage/postgres, re-run 2026-11-05). The recording fake shows the single UPDATE binds only on session_hash with catalog membership checks; no term ties the pair to the row's stored tenant/workspace or subject_id_hash.

remediation.strategy: Add the membership conjunction to the switch UPDATE's WHERE clause: keep the session's own tenant_id equal to the request tenant, and gate the target pair on the schema's grant tables (tenant_scope_grants keyed on tenant_id, workspace_id, scope_id, subject_class), extending the recording-fake test to pin the new terms.

code_changes.fixed_code:
WHERE sess.session_hash = $1
  AND sess.revoked_at IS NULL
  AND sess.tenant_id = $2
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tenant_scope_grants g
    WHERE g.tenant_id = $2
      AND g.workspace_id = $3
      AND g.subject_class = sess.subject_class
      AND g.tombstoned_at IS NULL
  )

likelihood.reason: Every context switch through this route takes the unbound path; the catalog check is the only gate.

impact.reason: The active anchor for later identity-bound reads can diverge from the row's own membership; scope stays inside the catalog-validated pair set.

confidence.reason: The recording fake captures the exact statement text, and the handler, switch query, resolve re-anchor, and the in-tree residual note were read at the cited lines on the reviewed tree; the pinned test re-ran green at HEAD.

title: MCP JSON-RPC request bodies decode without a byte cap, unlike the sibling intake decoder
description: The MCP request path decodes bodies with json.Decoder directly: handleHTTPMessage / handleMessage (go/internal/mcp/server.go:259-306) and the SSE-plane decode at go/internal/mcp/server_sse.go:240, both funnelling through querycontract.ReadJSON (go/internal/query/querycontract/http.go:105) with no http.MaxBytesReader. rg over go/internal/mcp shows zero MaxBytesReader hits. The sibling webhook intake decoder carries a 1 MiB cap with a 413 response, so the two JSON planes diverge. A 10 MiB body is retained in full; the 10 MiB retention is bounded only by that observed ceiling of the harness, since no cap exists in code.
root_cause: The MCP decoders never wrap r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader, so the stdlib parser buffers the entire supplied body.
intended_behavior: Both JSON planes decode under a declared bound and answer a clear 413-style error past it, matching the intake plane's contract.

trace.description: JSON-RPC dispatch entry for POST /mcp/message.
Bare json.Decoder over r.Body with no MaxBytesReader wrapper.

evidence.description: RunHTTP sets only header/write/idle timeouts; no body byte bound.
SSE-plane decode shares the uncapped helper.
Sibling intake decoder caps at 1 MiB with 413, the parity contract.

conditions.description: Reaching handleMessage requires the transport-auth or query gate already in front of it.
One JSON-RPC body larger than the sibling 1 MiB ceiling.

execution.attacker_perspective: An authenticated JSON-RPC caller on POST /mcp/message.
payloads: 10,485,760-byte JSON body (10 MiB) as a JSON-RPC message
instructions: Run a scratch _test.go over ./internal/mcp with -overlay: decode the 10 MiB body through the production helper and through InProcessMessageHandler.
execution.observed_result: PASS 0.133s: ReadJSON retained the full 10,485,760-byte value (10x the sibling cap, ~40x the 256 KiB response budget); POST /mcp/message answered 200 {result:{}} on the 10 MiB body with no 413 branch; non-JSON body gave 400 -32700; zero MaxBytesReader hits under go/internal/mcp.

remediation.strategy: Wrap r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader with the same 1 MiB ceiling the intake plane uses, at both MCP decode sites.

likelihood.reason: Only authenticated callers on the MCP plane can push bodies; per-request retention is linear in body size.

impact.reason: Heap retention per in-flight request bounded by the supplied body; released after decode.

confidence.reason: Executed scratch test through the production decoders plus an rg census of the package; both arms ran green.

title: Reducer graph read facet Run applies no transaction timeout while every write facet does
description: In go/cmd/reducer/neo4j_wiring.go the write facets pass the ESHU_CANONICAL_WRITE_TIMEOUT-derived bound - RunCypher at :56, RunCypherGroup at :102, QueryCypherExists at :168 via r.transactionConfigurers() - but the GraphQuery read facet Run (:181-211) calls session.Run(ctx, cypher, params) with no configurers, and transactionConfigurers returns nil for TxTimeout<=0 (:106-111). The pinned driver (v5.28.4) defaults its transaction timeout to math.MinInt meaning 'server default' and sends no tx_timeout BEGIN meta when no configurer is applied, so outside the repo only the server-side hint can bind the read. Meanwhile the heartbeat goroutine (go/internal/reducer/service_heartbeat.go:91-128) keeps renewing claim_until, so the expired-lease reclaim never fires and a wedged read pins its worker and pooled connection. The repo-dependency side lane (go/internal/reducer/repo_dependency_projection_runner.go:226) is the one read path with a client deadline; the main claim/execute/ack loop (go/internal/reducer/service.go:299-330) adds none.
root_cause: Run omits the r.transactionConfigurers() spread that every sibling facet passes, leaving its transaction on the driver's unbounded default.
intended_behavior: Every reducer graph round trip carries the same bounded transaction deadline as the write facets, or a parity test grades the read facet.

trace.description: Reducer bootstrap wires the session runner and the claim loop.
GraphQuery read facet calls session.Run without configurers.
session.Run(ctx, cypher, params) executes with no tx_timeout meta while siblings at :56/:102/:168 carry the bound.

evidence.description: transactionConfigurers returns nil when TxTimeout<=0, the state Run inherits.
TestReducerNeo4jSessionRunnerTransactionConfigurersSetTimeout and the QueryCypherExists parity test pass without covering the Run facet.
Heartbeat renews claim_until, so the expired-lease reclaim cannot free a wedged read.

conditions.description: A graph backend whose round trip stalls (slow query, paused server, network wedge).
Standard reducer deployment; the side-lane deadline exists only on the repo-dependency projection path.

execution.attacker_perspective: The reducer process itself against its pinned graph backend.
payloads: Scratch replication of transactionConfigurers for TxTimeout=0 and 4s
instructions: Run go test ./cmd/reducer -count=1.
Run a scratch main replicating neo4j_wiring.go:106-111 and assert nil vs one configurer.
execution.observed_result: Package suite ok 12.684s exit 0; scratch replication returned nil configurers for TxTimeout=0 and one configurer for 4s; the asymmetry between Run and its three siblings verified line by line (artifact agents/verifier-redread/artifacts/txconf_check.go).

remediation.strategy: Pass r.transactionConfigurers()... into the Run call so the read facet shares the same bound as the write facets.

code_changes.fixed_code: result, err := session.Run(ctx, cypher, params, r.transactionConfigurers()...)

likelihood.reason: Any stalled round trip on the read facet leaves no client-side deadline; the heartbeat keeps the claim alive.

impact.reason: One worker plus one pooled connection pinned per stuck read; the server-side hint may still bound it; queue progress resumes once the read returns.

confidence.reason: Facet-by-facet source comparison plus a scratch replication of the configurer derivation; driver default settled from the pinned module cache.

title: ESHU_REDUCER_HANDLER_TIMEOUT is loaded but never enforced on the handler execution path
description: main.go loads and validates ESHU_REDUCER_HANDLER_TIMEOUT and ESHU_REDUCER_HANDLER_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDES (go/cmd/reducer/main.go:218-232, stored at :455-456) and logs that they are recorded but not enforced yet. The only resolver, HandlerTimeoutFor (go/internal/reducer/service_heartbeat.go:245), has zero non-test callers. executeHandler (:292-331) selects on handler completion or shutdownCtx.Done() only, with a non-blocking second check at :324-328, so a stuck handler pins its worker, its pooled connection, and its fenced conflict key until process shutdown; the heartbeat keeps claim_until fresh so the expired-lease reclaim cannot fire. The batch caller (go/internal/reducer/service_batch.go:489) adds no bound either.
root_cause: The resolver exists but no execution path consumes it, so the operator-configured handler bound never reaches the select in executeHandler.
intended_behavior: The configured timeout bounds each handler execution, releasing the worker, connection, and conflict key at the declared bound, or the startup log states the exact non-enforced semantics.

trace.description: Loads and validates the timeout env vars and logs them as not yet enforced.
The only resolver of the stored bounds; callers are tests only.
Select with exactly two branches (done, shutdownCtx.Done()); no timeout case.

evidence.description: Startup WARN states the bounds are recorded but not enforced.
The only HandlerTimeoutFor callers; behavior otherwise ungraded.
Documented rows match the non-enforced posture.

conditions.description: A handler that blocks longer than the operator's intended bound (wedged backend round trip, long scan).
Deployment that sets ESHU_REDUCER_HANDLER_TIMEOUT or its overrides expecting enforcement.

execution.attacker_perspective: The operator observing queue progress with a stuck handler.
payloads: ESHU_REDUCER_HANDLER_TIMEOUT=2s with a handler that blocks
instructions: Run go test ./internal/reducer -run 'TestServiceRun|TestHandlerTimeoutFor' -count=1 -v.
rg for non-test callers of HandlerTimeoutFor.
execution.observed_result: exit 0: TestServiceRunAbandonsStuckHandlerAtShutdown, TestServiceRunBatchAbandonsStuckHandlerAtShutdown, TestHandlerTimeoutForResolvesOverrideThenDefault all PASS; rg shows zero non-test callers; the executeHandler select carries no timeout branch.

remediation.strategy: Apply the resolved bound inside executeHandler with a third select case on the timer, and abandon the item per the existing shutdown-abandon path on expiry.

likelihood.reason: Any stalled handler takes the unbounded path; the gap is structural, not input-dependent.

impact.reason: Per stuck handler: one worker, one pooled connection, and one fenced conflict key pinned until shutdown; other domains keep progressing.

confidence.reason: Focused tests re-run green, caller census and select shape read directly at the cited lines; startup WARN and README corroborate.

title: reducerWorkItemID is not prefix-free, so distinct intents collapse onto one work_item_id
description: reducerWorkItemID (go/internal/storage/postgres/reducer_queue_helpers.go:344-362) trims each part, rewrites ':' and '/' to '_', and joins only the non-empty parts with underscores, so adjacent fields lose their separator. Two collapse channels were reproduced: the hunter pair (domain 'aws_resource_materialization' with entity_key 'aws_resource_materialization_repo_a_b'-style suffixes) both print the identical id, and the slash/colon entity-key pair 'repo:y/src_main.go' vs 'repo:y/src:main.go' also collides; a tuple with an empty EntityKey collapses onto the 3-part layout (:354 drops empty parts). Because enqueue uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on work_item_id, a collapsed second intent is silently skipped. TestReducerWorkItemIDSanitizesSpecialChars (reducer_queue_test.go:35) pins single-tuple sanitization only, so injectivity is ungraded. Real-world density stays low: the reducercontract domain enum is closed and entity keys are constructed as domain+':'+scope; a lost intent self-heals on the next generation/replay.
root_cause: Joining sanitized parts with '_' without escaping produces a non-injective mapping from tuples to ids.
intended_behavior: Distinct (scope_id, generation_id, domain, entity_key) tuples map to distinct work_item_ids so ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING skips only true repeats.

trace.description: Enqueue derives work_item_id via reducerWorkItemID before the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert.
Trim, character rewrite, and join produce equal ids for distinct tuples at part boundaries.

evidence.description: Empty parts dropped, collapsing the 4-part layout onto the 3-part one.
Only single-tuple sanitization is pinned; no injectivity test exists.

conditions.description: Two intents whose sanitized parts align at a boundary (adjacent-field bleed or the '/'-vs-':' entity-key pair).

instructions: Scratch main calling the same sanitization/join and printing equality for the three cases.
Run go test ./internal/storage/postgres -run 'TestReducerQueue|TestClaimBatch|TestAckBatch' -count=1.
execution.observed_result: Both collapse channels reproduced verbatim: the hunter pair both print reducer_repo_a_b_g_aws_resource_materialization_aws_resource_materialization_repo_a_b (equal=true); the slash/colon pair collides; empty EntityKey collapses onto the 3-part layout. Suite ok 0.268s exit 0.

title: Recovery admin handlers decode JSON bodies without a byte cap while the sibling admin handler caps at 64 KiB
description: The three RecoveryHandler routes decode r.Body with json.NewDecoder directly (go/internal/runtime/recovery_handler.go:87, :146, :220) while the sibling legacy-workload-retirement handler caps at 64 KiB via http.MaxBytesReader (go/internal/runtime/legacy_workload_retirement_handler.go:71). The status listener binds ESHU_LISTEN_ADDR with default 0.0.0.0:8080 (go/internal/runtime/config.go:26), not loopback-only, and the plane sets ReadHeaderTimeout only (go/internal/runtime/http_server.go:64). With filter.Limit==0 selecting the no-SQL-LIMIT template (go/internal/storage/postgres/recovery.go:184-187), one request both inflates the heap through the uncapped decode and touches the whole queue table. The ingester binary is the sole WithRecoveryHandler caller (go/cmd/ingester/main.go:165). No element ceilings exist in the three filter Validate methods (go/internal/recovery/replay.go:93-101, :214-230, :307-312).
root_cause: The recovery decoders never wrap r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader, unlike the sibling handler that defines the plane's own contract.
intended_behavior: Every operator-plane JSON body decodes under a declared bound with a clear over-limit error, matching the 64 KiB sibling.

trace.description: Sole WithRecoveryHandler caller mounting the three admin routes on the status plane.
Bare json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode with no MaxBytesReader; :87 and :146 repeat the shape.

evidence.description: First bare decode.
Sibling caps at 64<<10 and answers 400 past it - the parity contract.
Limit==0 selects the statement with no SQL LIMIT.

conditions.description: Reachability of the status listener; default bind 0.0.0.0:8080.
A refinalize body of ~4.4 MB (300k scope ids) or a filter with Limit==0.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any client that can reach the status listener.
payloads: Same body through the 64 KiB-capped shape as the control
instructions: Run the scratch decodecap test over ./internal/runtime.
Run go test ./internal/runtime/ -count=1 -run Recovery|Refinalize|Replay.
execution.observed_result: Bare-decoder shape: status 200, decoded_ids=300000, heap delta 17,727,896 B. Capped shape: 400 request body too large, heap delta 261,680 B. Recovery/refinalize/replay suite PASS incl. TestNewStatusAdminServerWithoutRecoveryReturns404ForRecoveryRoutes; exit 0 (artifact agents/verifier-recovery/artifacts/decodecap_test.go).

remediation.strategy: Wrap each recovery decode in http.MaxBytesReader with the 64 KiB sibling bound, and give the three filter Validate methods element ceilings consistent with the response budget.

likelihood.reason: Admin-plane routes only, reached by configured operators and the ingester itself.

impact.reason: Per-request heap inflation (~17.7 MB measured at 4.4 MB body) and one full-table scan; both release after the request.

confidence.reason: Independent scratch harness reproduced both the uncapped and capped deltas; cited sites read directly; package suite green.
